title: Grab And Move Horizontal Move Unlocks Vertically Maximized Window
author: KorayL
summary: Grab and Move follows the pointer exactly and therefore restores a vertically maximized window when the drag includes vertical movement; matching native title-bar tolerance would be a feature request.
next_action: Close as expected behavior unless maintainers want a separately scoped enhancement for preserving vertical maximization.

confidence.rationale: The public discussion and linked ownership evidence support this classification.

judgment.rationale: Grab and Move directly translates a window under the pointer and does not emulate Windows' title-bar tolerance for preserving a vertically maximized state. The only maintainer-side response identifies the observed unmaximize behavior as normal Windows dragging semantics.
evidence: The issue reproduces only after vertically maximizing and then introducing vertical pointer movement during a horizontal Grab and Move.
The requested tolerance matches native title-bar drag behavior rather than an existing documented Grab and Move guarantee.
A collaborator states that the result sounds like default Windows behavior.
judgment.recommended_action: Close as expected behavior unless maintainers want a separately scoped enhancement for preserving vertical maximization.

fix_assessment.rationale: The report describes current direct-drag behavior; preserving vertical maximization would be a new feature rather than a bug fix.

issue_context.summary: Grab and Move follows the pointer exactly and therefore restores a vertically maximized window when the drag includes vertical movement; matching native title-bar tolerance would be a feature request.
known_information: A slight vertical component during Grab and Move restores the window.
inferences: Preserving vertical maximization would require explicit snap-state tracking and tolerance logic not promised by the current utility.
issue_context.analysis: There is no evidence of state corruption or failure outside the direct-move semantics. The issue should be reframed as an enhancement if the behavior is desired.
initial_investigation: Reviewed the complete live report, collaborator response, labels, and timeline.
Found no conflicting reproduction or linked regression.

actions.label: Close as expected drag behavior
actions.note: Draft only; no comment, close, label, or other write was made to microsoft/PowerToys.

comment.body: Grab and Move currently translates the window with the pointer and does not apply the title-bar drag tolerance that preserves Windows' vertically maximized state. The reported restore when the pointer moves vertically is therefore expected for the current utility. If preserving vertical maximization is desired, it should be tracked as a separately scoped enhancement with the preferred movement tolerance.
